title: Tiered Behavior Templates — Scratchbook
body:
Purpose / quick note:
This is a personal scratchbook for a lightweight feature: Tiered Behavior Templates (TBT). Idea: let apps pick a named "behavior" for assistant responses (e.g., terse, balanced, pedagogical) that maps to a bundle of runtime knobs (model variant, temperature, max tokens, response-length constraints, compression policy, caching priority). Primary goal: give product/UX teams an easy knob to trade cost vs. helpfulness without forcing low-level config on devs or end users.

Why this?
- Product teams repeatedly ask for simple presets for cost/quality control.
- Current approach = docs + examples + separate model routing rules; messy and error-prone.
- A first-class, named template can be exposed in Console, API, and embedded into UI flows.

Quick sketch of concept:
- Template = {name, description, priority_tier, routing_profile, transformation_profile, telemetry_tags}
- priority_tier: one of [economy, standard, premium] — influences routing fallback and queue priority.
- routing_profile: preferred model family + allowed fallbacks (e.g., Llama-70B-qat -> Llama-13B-quant 
- transformation_profile: length limits, stop heuristics, summarization-wrapping, verbosity_target (short/medium/long), answer-style (formal/colloquial)
- telemetry_tags: hooks for cost attribution and evals (e.g., template:economy_v1)

User stories (draft):
- As a product engineer, I can attach a template to an endpoint so that front-end devs can pick a label ("concise") instead of tuning tokens/temperature.
- As an end-user, I can set my assistant preference to "detailed" in settings and get longer, more explanatory answers.
- As an infra/operator, I can route "economy" templates to dedicated cheaper pools and apply stricter timeouts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: create/edit list of templates (name + short desc + pick from simple radio options).
- API: endpoint accepts template=name; request logs include template tag.
- Runtime: template maps to at least 3 runtime knobs (model variant, max_output_tokens, compression_rule).
- Observability: dashboard shows token/cost broken down by template tag.

Example templates (very rough):
- Whisper: "economy" — model: small-quant; temp: 0.2; max_tokens: 120; verbosity: short; fallback: truncate+summarize; priority: low
- Compass: "standard" — model: base-quant; temp: 0.6; max_tokens: 512; verbosity: medium; priority: normal
- Lighthouse: "premium" — model: opt-bert-compat; temp: 0.8; max_tokens: 2048; verbosity: long; caching: bypass; priority: high

Notes to self on mapping to Redwood product surfaces:
- Hosted API: expose templates as top-level param: "behavior_template": "compass_v1". Docs + examples.
- Dedicated: map templates to reserved pools via routing rules in Dedicated config. Policy: template.priority -> pool.capability.
- Private: templates live in customer-managed config; provide a CLI import/export.

Runtime implications / heuristics to consider:
- Templates can be soft (suggested knobs) or hard (enforced). MVP should do soft plus server-side enforcement of token cap.
- When model fallback happens, we should auto-adjust verbosity targets (i.e., if downgrading to smaller model, reduce max_tokens and increase compression).
- Caching: template tag allows prefetching / prefix caching policies. e.g., premium templates might bypass caching to always prefer fresh computations. economy templates prefer cached partials.

Metric hypotheses to validate:
- Economy templates reduce per-request median token cost by X% (target 30%).
- Premium templates increase user satisfaction (NPS/qual) for power users — need small pilot.
- Adoption metric: % endpoints using templates after 6 weeks.

Experiment plan (alpha):
- 2-week internal alpha: pick 3 Redwood internal apps (docs-summarizer, support-bot, sales-assistant). Provide them with 2 templates (economy_v1, standard_v1).
- Measure: token cost, latency p95, & manual quality checks on 50 sample prompts (blind eval).

Open questions / risks:
- UX naming: avoid brandy names — should be descriptive for users ("concise", "detailed"). Marketing might want cute names.
- How to represent multi-dimensional tradeoffs in a single label without confusing users? Provide inline tooltip with sample output size/epochs.
- Billing/attribution: should templates be charged differently or just surface cost estimates? Need finance consult (JIRA INF-5421).
- Security: could templates accidentally enable bypasses (e.g., unrestricted context size) — ensure RBAC for template creation in orgs.

Implementation roadmap (quick):
- Week 1: proto data model + Console list UI (read-only)
